Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

Observed facts: The patient had follicular lymphoma followed by high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC, BCL2 and BCL6 alterations and marrow involvement. Six cycles of R-mini-CHOP produced a mixed response with new liver lesions. Clavicular and periportal samples were negative for lymphoma. The liver biopsy expressed histiocytic/dendritic markers rather than B-cell markers. MYC and BCL2 abnormalities overlapped with earlier material. Clonality testing on the original follicular lymphoma was not completed. The material does not securely establish one precise histiocytic/dendritic subtype.

Hypotheses (not established): The overlapping MYC and BCL2 abnormalities raise the possibility of a shared clonal origin between the B-cell neoplasm and the histiocytic/dendritic lesion, suggesting transdifferentiation. However, without completed clonality studies on the original follicular lymphoma, this remains unproven. The negative clavicular and periportal samples argue against widespread lymphoma but do not exclude a lineage-switch process confined to the liver.

Proposed actions: Expert haematopathology review comparing the original B-cell material with the liver biopsy is needed to assess whether the overlapping genetic abnormalities reflect a true clonal relationship or coincidental findings. If available, immunohistochemistry panels distinguishing specific histiocytic/dendritic subtypes should be applied.
